scope: Third architecture review: local feature-contract alignment and internal consistency across seven architecture specs and adjacent indexes. No host API/version certification or runtime implementation audit.
prior_findings: The previous three corrections remain addressed: spec new inputs, prospective index snapshots, and completed-step rerun recording.

findings.title: Restrict setup and failure cleanup to a worktree created by this invocation
findings.finding: createWorktree explicitly reuses an existing worktree, but Start step 6 unconditionally runs setup_hook after that call and force-removes the worktree on failure, asserting it is fresh. On resume this can rerun setup in a retained checkout and delete its uncommitted work. The feature requires setup only for a newly created worktree; the general preservation rule does not resolve this contradictory specific procedure.
findings.recommendation: Return or track whether this invocation created the worktree. Run setup and rollback removal only for that newly created checkout; preserve reused checkouts. Distinguish resuming with an existing worktree from recreating a missing one.
verification_required: Resume an existing dirty worktree with a failing configured setup hook: hook is not invoked and all bytes are retained.
Resume a retained branch with a missing checkout: create the worktree and run setup once.
A fresh creation with a failing setup hook removes only the newly created checkout.

findings.title: Expose a lease-bound test execution request through the core and Codex runner
findings.finding: The runner accepts only inspect, prepare, validate, record, capture, cancel and close, rejecting unknown methods. The shared boundary requires tests launched by core under the active workflow lease and matched to its private execution ledger. Neither the public export/operation inventory nor the runner defines how the existing session requests that execution after its edits. Shell-run tests cannot meet that receipt contract, so a test-bearing step has no specified path to a valid done result through the advertised runner.
findings.recommendation: Define a typed execution request/result and public core operation, then expose it through the persistent runner under the prepared request and existing lease. Specify allowed executable/argument/report inputs, cancellation, state binding and the returned artifact reference. Keep the separately labelled manual fallback distinct.
verification_required: Drive prepare, implementation edits, core-owned test execution, validate and record through the documented runner protocol.
Verify stale state, cancellation and forged receipts are rejected and a failed test cannot produce done.
